line: Lenovo ThinkPad T14s Gen 7 (2026, Intel Panther Lake)
config_name: ThinkPad T14s Gen 7 — Core Ultra 5 325, 32GB LPDDR5X, 512GB SSD, 14" WUXGA IPS 400-nit non-touch

specs.cpu: Intel Core Ultra 5 325 (Panther Lake, LPE-cores up to 3.4 GHz, P-cores up to 4.5 GHz)
specs.keyboard_notes: ThinkPad keyboard 1.5mm travel, TrackPoint, auto backlit

battery.notes: 58Wh. NBC measured ~17.5h Wi-Fi test on AMD sibling; Panther Lake Ultra 5 is comparable-to-slightly-better at light load.

price.notes: Intel T14s Gen 7 CTO on lenovo.com/ca; estimated from AMD CTO base ($2,093.55 verified) + Intel Ultra 5 tier delta. Lenovo CA runs eCoupon-stacked pricing.

reviews.quote: Both the AMD and Intel SKUs offer pretty much the same level of performance and you still get a good keyboard (even though it could be better) and a decent number of ports with a new USB-C port on the right side.

praises: Intel variant gets the full 320 MHz Wi-Fi 7 radio (NBC measured ~3.9 Gbps vs 1.7 Gbps on the AMD MediaTek card)
NBC found AMD and Intel SKUs perform about the same — pick whichever is on sale
Thunderbolt 4 is native on Intel SKUs for docking compatibility with older TB docks
Same light redesigned 1.19 kg chassis, replaceable SSD/battery/WWAN as the AMD model
32GB standard on Intel prebuys — no 16GB trap at this tier
complaints: Ultra 5 325's 4-Xe3 iGPU is the weakest graphics option in the line (Cyberpunk ~20 fps 1080p low in sibling test)
Base WUXGA 400-nit 45% NTSC panel again — colour work needs the OLED CTO
Soldered RAM, same as every T14s Gen 7 SKU
60 Hz only on all IPS panels
Intel CTO pricing on lenovo.com/ca is volatile with rotating eCoupons

design_philosophy: The Intel platform option of the T14s fleet line — identical chassis, keyboard, and battery as the AMD model, chosen by IT shops for native Thunderbolt and Intel vPro manageability. The Ultra 5 tier is the price-conscious fleet SKU.
rating_notes: Inferred from Notebookcheck's T14s Gen 7 AMD review (90%) plus NBC's note that AMD and Intel SKUs perform about the same; Ultra 5 325 tier → productivity −0.5 and gaming 3.0 (4-Xe3 iGPU, per sibling T14 Gen 7 benchmarks). Intel BE211 supports the port_connectivity/docking note. Price estimated (CA Intel CTO page not directly fetched); image URL from the verified AMD CDN path as fallback.
